**Barcelona**[[a]](#cite_note-8) is a city on the northeastern coast of [Spain](/wiki/Spain "Spain"). It is the capital and largest city of the [autonomous community](/wiki/Autonomous_communities_of_Spain "Autonomous communities of Spain") of [Catalonia](/wiki/Catalonia "Catalonia"), as well as the second-most populous municipality of Spain. With a population of 1.7 million within city limits,[[3]](#cite_note-population-3) its urban area extends to numerous neighbouring municipalities within the [province of Barcelona](/wiki/Province_of_Barcelona "Province of Barcelona") and is home to around 5.7 million people,[[4]](#cite_note-demographia-4) making it the [fifth most populous urban area](/wiki/List_of_urban_areas_in_the_European_Union "List of urban areas in the European Union") of the [European Union](/wiki/European_Union "European Union") after [Paris](/wiki/Paris "Paris"), the [Ruhr](/wiki/Ruhr "Ruhr") area, [Madrid](/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") and [Milan](/wiki/Milan "Milan").[[4]](#cite_note-demographia-4) It is one of the largest metropolises on the [Mediterranean Sea](/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea "Mediterranean Sea"), located on the coast between the mouths of the rivers [Llobregat](/wiki/Llobregat "Llobregat") and [Besòs](/wiki/Bes%C3%B2s_(river) "Besòs (river)"), bounded to the west by the [Serra de Collserola](/wiki/Serra_de_Collserola "Serra de Collserola") mountain range.

Taylor again retired from the Army on 1 July 1964, having been succeeded as Chairman of the Joint Chief of Staff by General [Earle Wheeler](/wiki/Earle_Wheeler "Earle Wheeler"), and became [Ambassador to South Vietnam](/wiki/United_States_Ambassador_to_South_Vietnam "United States Ambassador to South Vietnam") from 1964 to 1965, succeeding [Henry Cabot Lodge Jr.](/wiki/Henry_Cabot_Lodge_Jr. "Henry Cabot Lodge Jr.") Taylor served in the Pentagon during parts of 1965 as "SACSA", the Special Advisor for Counterinsurgency Affairs". He was Special Consultant to the President and Chairman of the [Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board](/wiki/President%27s_Foreign_Intelligence_Advisory_Board "President's Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board") (1965–1969) and President of the [Institute for Defense Analyses](/wiki/Institute_for_Defense_Analyses "Institute for Defense Analyses") (1966–1969).

Afflicted with [amyotrophic lateral sclerosis](/wiki/Amyotrophic_lateral_sclerosis "Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis") (also called "[Lou Gehrig's disease](/wiki/Lou_Gehrig#Illness "Lou Gehrig")"), Taylor spent his last three months at [Walter Reed Army Medical Center](/wiki/Walter_Reed_Army_Medical_Center "Walter Reed Army Medical Center") in [Washington, DC](/wiki/Washington,_DC "Washington, DC"), and died at 85 years of age on April 19, 1987.[[1]](#cite_note-srvapobt-1) He was interred at [Arlington National Cemetery](/wiki/Arlington_National_Cemetery "Arlington National Cemetery").[[30]](#cite_note-30)

The first-ever long-distance subscriber trunk dialing (STD) call in India was made between the cities of Kanpur and Lucknow in 1960.

The total length of all phone numbers (area code and the phone number) is constant at 10 digits. For example, the number 7513200000 signifies the area code 751 (the area code for [Gwalior](/wiki/Gwalior "Gwalior")) followed by the phone number.

Fixed-line or landline numbers are at most 8 digits long.

With two minutes remaining, Hrubesch headed the winner for West Germany from a [Karl-Heinz Rummenigge](/wiki/Karl-Heinz_Rummenigge "Karl-Heinz Rummenigge") [corner](/wiki/Corner_kick "Corner kick").[[35]](#cite_note-35)

An estimated 2.56 million tonnes of inland fish and other aquatic animals are consumed in the lower Mekong every year.[[54]](#cite_note-MRC_2010b-55) Aquatic resources make up between 47 and 80% of animal protein in rural diets for people who live in the Lower Mekong Basin.[[56]](#cite_note-Baran&Ratner2007-57)[[59]](#cite_note-Bush2003-60)[[60]](#cite_note-Friend&Blake2009-61) Fish are the cheapest source of animal protein in the region and any decline in the fishery is likely to significantly impact nutrition, especially among the poor.[[50]](#cite_note-ICEM2010-51)[[59]](#cite_note-Bush2003-60)[[61]](#cite_note-Baird_2009a-62)[[62]](#cite_note-Baird_2011-63) Fish are the staple of the diet in Laos and Cambodia, with around 80% of the Cambodian population's annual protein intake coming from fish caught in the Mekong River system, with no alternative source to replace it. An MRC report claims that dam projects on the Mekong River will reduce aquatic life by 40% by 2020, and predicted that 80% of fish will be depleted by 2040. Thailand will be impacted, as its fish stocks in the Mekong will decline by 55%, Laos will be reduced by 50%, Cambodia by 35%, and Vietnam by 30%.[[63]](#cite_note-BP-20190720-64)

It is estimated that 40 million rural people, more than two-thirds of the rural population in the lower Mekong basin, are engaged in the wild capture fishery.[[4]](#cite_note-MRC_2010a-5) Fisheries contribute significantly to a diversified livelihood strategy for many people, particularly the poor, who are highly dependent on the river and its resources for their livelihoods.[[55]](#cite_note-Baran&Myschowoda2009-56)[[56]](#cite_note-Baran&Ratner2007-57)[[60]](#cite_note-Friend&Blake2009-61) They provide a principal form of income for numerous people and act as a safety net and coping strategy in times of poor agricultural harvests or other difficulties.[[55]](#cite_note-Baran&Myschowoda2009-56)[[56]](#cite_note-Baran&Ratner2007-57)[[60]](#cite_note-Friend&Blake2009-61) In Laos alone, 71% of rural households (2.9 million people) rely on fisheries for either subsistence or additional cash income.
